sourceChapterWithLineNumbers:
1:   Arjuna.
2:   Who is that BRAHMA? What that Soul of Souls,
3:   The ADHYATMAN? What, Thou Best of All!
4:   Thy work, the KARMA? Tell me what it is
5:   Thou namest ADHIBHUTA? What again
6:   Means ADHIDAIVA? Yea, and how it comes
7:   Thou canst be ADHIYAJNA in thy flesh?
8:   Slayer of Madhu! Further, make me know
9:   How good men find thee in the hour of death?
10: 
11:   Krishna.
12:   I BRAHMA am! the One Eternal GOD,
13:   And ADHYATMAN is My Being's name,
14:   The Soul of Souls! What goeth forth from Me,
15:   Causing all life to live, is KARMA called:
16:   And, Manifested in divided forms,
17:   I am the ADHIBHUTA, Lord of Lives;
18:   And ADHIDAIVA, Lord of all the Gods,
19:   Because I am PURUSHA, who begets.
20:   And ADHIYAJNA, Lord of Sacrifice,
21:   I--speaking with thee in this body here--
22:   Am, thou embodied one! (for all the shrines
23:   Flame unto Me!) And, at the hour of death,
24:   He that hath meditated Me alone,
25:   In putting off his flesh, comes forth to Me,
26:   Enters into My Being--doubt thou not!
27:   But, if he meditated otherwise
28:   At hour of death, in putting off the flesh,
29:   He goes to what he looked for, Kunti's Son!
30:   Because the Soul is fashioned to its like.
31: 
32:   Have Me, then, in thy heart always! and fight!
33:   Thou too, when heart and mind are fixed on Me,
34:   Shalt surely come to Me! All come who cleave
35:   With never-wavering will of firmest faith,
36:   Owning none other Gods: all come to Me,
37:   The Uttermost, Purusha, Holiest!
38: 
39:   Whoso hath known Me, Lord of sage and singer,
40:      Ancient of days; of all the Three Worlds Stay,
41:   Boundless,--but unto every atom Bringer
42:      Of that which quickens it: whoso, I say,
43: 
44:   Hath known My form, which passeth mortal knowing;
45:     Seen my effulgence--which no eye hath seen--
46:   Than the sun's burning gold more brightly glowing,
47:     Dispersing darkness,--unto him hath been
48: 
49:   Right life! And, in the hour when life is ending,
50:     With mind set fast and trustful piety,
51:   Drawing still breath beneath calm brows unbending,
52:     In happy peace that faithful one doth die,--
53: 
54:   In glad peace passeth to Purusha's heaven.
55:      The place which they who read the Vedas name
56:   AKSHARAM, "Ultimate;" whereto have striven
57:      Saints and ascetics--their road is the same.
58: 
59:   That way--the highest way--goes he who shuts
60:   The gates of all his senses, locks desire
61:   Safe in his heart, centres the vital airs
62:   Upon his parting thought, steadfastly set;
63:   And, murmuring OM, the sacred syllable--
64:   Emblem of BRAHM--dies, meditating Me.
65: 
66:   For who, none other Gods regarding, looks
67:   Ever to Me, easily am I gained
68:   By such a Yogi; and, attaining Me,
69:   They fall not--those Mahatmas--back to birth,
70:   To life, which is the place of pain, which ends,
71:   But take the way of utmost blessedness.
72: 
73:   The worlds, Arjuna!--even Brahma's world--
74:   Roll back again from Death to Life's unrest;
75:   But they, O Kunti's Son! that reach to Me,
76:   Taste birth no more. If ye know Brahma's Day
77:   Which is a thousand Yugas; if ye know
78:   The thousand Yugas making Brahma's Night,
79:   Then know ye Day and Night as He doth know!
80:   When that vast Dawn doth break, th' Invisible
81:   Is brought anew into the Visible;
82:   When that deep Night doth darken, all which is
83:   Fades back again to Him Who sent it forth;
84:   Yea! this vast company of living things--
85:   Again and yet again produced--expires
86:   At Brahma's Nightfall; and, at Brahma's Dawn,
87:   Riseth, without its will, to life new-born.
88:   But--higher, deeper, innermost--abides
89:   Another Life, not like the life of sense,
90:   Escaping sight, unchanging. This endures
91:   When all created things have passed away:
92:   This is that Life named the Unmanifest,
93:   The Infinite! the All! the Uttermost.
94:   Thither arriving none return. That Life
95:   Is Mine, and I am there! And, Prince! by faith
96:   Which wanders not, there is a way to come
97:   Thither. I, the PURUSHA, I Who spread
98:   The Universe around me--in Whom dwell
99:   All living Things--may so be reached and seen!
100: 
101:   .    .    .    .    .    .    .    .    .    .    .    .    .    . [FN#14]
102: 
103:   Richer than holy fruit on Vedas growing,
104:      Greater than gifts, better than prayer or fast,
105:   Such wisdom is! The Yogi, this way knowing,
106:      Comes to the Utmost Perfect Peace at last.
107: 
108:   HERE ENDETH CHAPTER VIII. OF THE  BHAGAVAD-GITA,
109:   Entitled  "Aksharaparabrahmayog,"
110:   Or "The book of Religion by Devotion to the One Supreme God."

arnold.content:
Yea, and how it comes
  Thou canst be ADHIYAJNA in thy flesh?
  Slayer of Madhu! Further, make me know
  How good men find thee in the hour of death?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.2 Who and how is Adhiyajna here in this body, O destroyer of Madhu (Krishna)? And how at the time of death, art Thou to be known by the self-controlled?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.2 Who is it who rules the spirit sacrifice in many; and at the time of death how may those who have learned self-control come to the knowledge of Thee?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.2 O Madhusudana, how, and who, is the entity existing in the sacrifice here in this body? And at the time of death, how are You to be known by people of concentrated minds?

records.sanskrit:

arnold.content:
Krishna.
  I BRAHMA am! the One Eternal GOD,
  And ADHYATMAN is My Being's name,
  The Soul of Souls! What goeth forth from Me,
  Causing all life to live, is KARMA called:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.3 The Blessed Lord said Brahman is the Imperishable, the Supreme; Its essential nature is called Self-knowledge; the offering (to the gods) which causes existence and manifestation of beings and which also sustains them is called action.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.3 The Lord Shri Krishna replied: The Supreme Spirit is the Highest Imperishable Self, and Its Nature is spiritual consciousness. The worlds have been created and are supported by an emanation from the Spirit which is called the Law.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.3 The Blessed Lord said The Immutable is the supreme Brahman; self-hood is said to the entity present in the individual plane. By action is meant the offerings which bring about the origin of the existence of things.

records.sanskrit:
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम्।
अधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर ॥
records.iast:
adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaścādhidaivatam
adhiyajño.ahamevātra dehe dehabhṛtāṃ vara
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And, Manifested in divided forms,
  I am the ADHIBHUTA, Lord of Lives;
  And ADHIDAIVA, Lord of all the Gods,
  Because I am PURUSHA, who begets.
  And ADHIYAJNA, Lord of Sacrifice,
  I--speaking with thee in this body here--
  Am, thou embodied one! (for all the shrines
  Flame unto Me!)

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.4 Adhibhuta (knowledge of the elements) pertains to My perishable Nature and the Purusha or the Soul is the Adhidaiva; I alone am the Adhiyajna here in this body, O best among the embodied (men).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.4 Matter consists of the forms that perish; Divinity is the Supreme Self; and He who inspires the spirit of sacrifice in man, O noblest of thy race, is I Myself, Who now stand in human form before thee.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.4 The which exists in the physical plane is the mutable entity, and what exists in the divine plane is the Person. O best among the embodied beings, I Myself am the entity that exists in the sacrifice in this body.

records.sanskrit:
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम्।
यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥
records.iast:
antakāle ca māmeva smaranmuktvā kalevaram
yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And, at the hour of death,
  He that hath meditated Me alone,
  In putting off his flesh, comes forth to Me,
  Enters into My Being--doubt thou not!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.5 And whosoever, leaving the body, goes forth remembering Me alone, at the time of death, he attains My Being: there is no doubt about this.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.5 Whosoever at the time of death thinks only of Me, and thinking thus leaves the body and goes forth, assuredly he will know Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.5 And at the time of death, anyone who departs by giving up the body while thinking of Me alone, he attains My state. There is no doubt about this.

records.sanskrit:
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम्।
तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥
records.iast:
yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram
taṃ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But, if he meditated otherwise
  At hour of death, in putting off the flesh,
  He goes to what he looked for, Kunti's Son!
  Because the Soul is fashioned to its like.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.6 Whosoever at the end leaves the body, thinking of any being, to that being only does he go, O son of Kunti (Arjuna), because of his constant thought of that being.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.6 On whatever sphere of being the mind of a man may be intent at the time of death, thither he will go.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.6 O son of Kunti, thinking of any entity whichever it may be one gives up the body at the end, he attains that very one, having been always engrossed in its thought.

records.sanskrit:
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयः (orसंशयम्) ॥
records.iast:
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca

records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Have Me, then, in thy heart always! and fight!
  Thou too, when heart and mind are fixed on Me,
  Shalt surely come to Me!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.7 Therefore at all times remember Me only and fight. With mind and intellect fixed (or absorbed) in Me, thou shalt doubtessly come to Me alone.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.7 Therefore meditate always on Me, and fight; if thy mind and thy reason be fixed on Me, to Me shalt thou surely come.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.7 Therefore, think of Me at all times and fight. There is no doubt that by dedicating your mind and intellect to Me, you will attain Me alone.

records.sanskrit:

records.iast:

records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
All come who cleave
  With never-wavering will of firmest faith,
  Owning none other Gods: all come to Me,
  The Uttermost, Purusha, Holiest!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.8 With the mind not moving towards any other thing, made steadfast by the method of habitual meditation, and constantly meditating, one goes to the Supreme Person, the Resplendent, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.8 He whose mind does not wander, and who is engaged in constant meditation, attains the Supreme Spirit.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.8 O son of Prtha, by meditating with a mind which is engaged in the yoga of practice and which does not stray away to anything else, one reaches the supreme Person existing in the effulgent region.

arnold.content:
Whoso hath known Me, Lord of sage and singer,
     Ancient of days; of all the Three Worlds Stay,
  Boundless,--but unto every atom Bringer
     Of that which quickens it: whoso, I say,

  Hath known My form, which passeth mortal knowing;
    Seen my effulgence--which no eye hath seen--
  Than the sun's burning gold more brightly glowing,
    Dispersing darkness,--unto him hath been

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.9 Whosoever meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, the Ruler (of the whole world), minuter than an atom, the supporter of all, of inconceivable form, effulgent like the sun and beyond the darkness of ignorance.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.9 Whoso meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, more minute than the atom, yet the Ruler and Upholder of all, Unimaginable, Brilliant like the Sun, Beyond the reach of darkness;

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.9 He who meditates on the Omniscient, the Anceint, the Ruler, subtler than the subtle, the Ordainer of everything, of inconceivable form, effulgent like the sun, and beyond darkness-(he attains the supreme Person).

records.sanskrit:

भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव।

records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Right life! And, in the hour when life is ending,
    With mind set fast and trustful piety,
  Drawing still breath beneath calm brows unbending,
    In happy peace that faithful one doth die,--

  In glad peace passeth to Purusha's heaven.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.10 At the time of death, with unshaken mind, endowed with devotio, by the power of Yoga, fixing the whole life-breath in the middle of the two eyrows, he reaches that resplendent Supreme Person.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.10 He who leaves the body with mind unmoved and filled with devotion, by the power of his meditation gathering between his eyebrows his whole vital energy, attains the Supreme.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.10 At the time of death, having fully fixed the Prana (vita force) between the enrows with an unswering mind, and being imbued with devotion as also the strength of concentration, he reaches that resplendent supreme person.

records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The place which they who read the Vedas name
  AKSHARAM, "Ultimate;" whereto have striven
     Saints and ascetics--their road is the same.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.11 That which is declared Imperishable by those who know the Vedas, that which the self-controlled (ascetics or Sannyasins) and passion-free enter, that desiring which celibacy is practised that goal I will declare to thee in brief.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.11 Now I will speak briefly of the imperishable goal, proclaimed by those versed in the scriptures, which the mystic attains when free from passion, and for which he is content to undergo the vow of continence.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.11 I shall speak to you briefly of that immutable Goal which the knowers of the Vedas declare, into which enter the deligent ones free from attachment, and aspiring for which people practise celibacy.

records.sanskrit:

मूध्न्यार्धायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम् ॥
records.iast:

records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
That way--the highest way--goes he who shuts
  The gates of all his senses, locks desire
  Safe in his heart, centres the vital airs
  Upon his parting thought, steadfastly set;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.12 Having closed all the gates, confined the mind in the heart and fixed the life-breath in the head, engaged in the practice of concentration.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.12 Closing the gates of the body, drawing the forces of his mind into the heart and by the power of meditation concentrating his vital energy in the brain;

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.12 Having controlled all the passages, having confined the mind in the heart, and having fixed his own vital force in the head, (and then) continuing in the firmness in yoga;

records.sanskrit:
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन्।
यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
records.iast:

records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And, murmuring OM, the sacred syllable--
  Emblem of BRAHM--dies, meditating Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.13 Uttering the one-syllabled Om the Brahman and remembering Me, he who departs, leaving the body, attains to the Supreme Goal.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.13 Repeating Om, the Symbol of Eternity, holding Me always in remembrance, he who thus leaves his body and goes forth reaches the Spirit Supreme.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.13 He who departs by leaving the body while uttering the single syllable, viz Om, which is Brahman, and thinking of Me, he attains the supreme Goal.

records.sanskrit:

तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
records.iast:
ananyacetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ
tasyāhaṃ sulabhaḥ pārtha nityayuktasya yoginaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.14 I am easily attainable by that ever-steadfast Yogi who constantly and daily remembers Me (for a long time), not thinking of anything else (with a single mind or one-pointed mind), O Partha (Arjuna).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.14 To him who thinks constantly of Me, and of nothing else, to such an ever-faithful devotee, O Arjuna, am I ever accessible.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.14 O son of Prtha, to that yogi of constant concentration and single-minded attention, who remembers Me uninterruptedly and for long, I am easy of attainment.

records.sanskrit:
मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम्।
नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥
records.iast:
māmupetya punarjanma duḥkhālayamaśāśvatam
nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
and, attaining Me,
  They fall not--those Mahatmas--back to birth,
  To life, which is the place of pain, which ends,
  But take the way of utmost blessedness.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text:
8.15 Having attained Me these great souls do not again take birth (here) which is the place of pain
and is non-eternal: they have reached the highest perfection (liberation).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.15 Coming thus unto Me, these great souls go no more to the misery and death of earthly life, for they have gained perfection.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.15 As a result of reaching Me, the exalted ones who have attained the highest perfection do not get rirth which is an abode of sorrows and which is impermanent.

records.sanskrit:
आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन।
मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥
records.iast:
ābrahmabhuvanāllokāḥ punarāvartino.arjuna
māmupetya tu kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The worlds, Arjuna!--even Brahma's world--
  Roll back again from Death to Life's unrest;
  But they, O Kunti's Son! that reach to Me,
  Taste birth no more.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.16 (All) the worlds including the world of Brahma are subject to return again, O Arjuna; but he who reaches Me, O son of Kunti, has no rirth.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.16 The worlds, with the whole realm of creation, come and go; but, O Arjuna, whoso comes to Me, for him there is nor rebirth.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.16 O Arjuna, all the worlds together with the world of Brahma are subject to return. But, O son of Kunti, there is no rirth after reaching Me.

records.sanskrit:
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद् ब्रह्मणो विदुः।
रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥
records.iast:
sahasrayugaparyantamaharyad brahmaṇo viduḥ
rātriṃ yugasahasrāntāṃ te.ahorātravido janāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
If ye know Brahma's Day
  Which is a thousand Yugas; if ye know
  The thousand Yugas making Brahma's Night,
  Then know ye Day and Night as He doth know!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.17 Those people who know the day of Brahma which is of a duration of a thousand Yugas (ages) and the night which is also of a thousand Yugas duration, they know day and night.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.17 Those who understand the cosmic day and cosmic night know that one day of creation is a thousand cycles, and that the night is of equal length.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.17 Those poeple who are knowers of what day and night are, know the day of Brahma which ends in a thousand yugas [The four yugas (in the human worlds), viz Satya, Treta, Dwapara, and Kali are made up of 4,320,000 years. This period multiplied by a thousand constitutes one day of Brahma. His night also extends over an eal period. See M.S. and V.S.A.], and His night which ends in a thousand yugas.

records.sanskrit:
अव्यक्ताद् व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे।
रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके ॥
records.iast:
avyaktād vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavantyaharāgame
rātryāgame pralīyante tatraivāvyaktasaṃjñake
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.18 From the Unmanifested all the manifested (worlds) proceed at the coming of the 'day'; at the coming of the 'night' they dissolve verily into ï1thatï1 alone which is called the Unmanifested.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.18 At the dawning of that day all objects in manifestation stream forth from the Unmanifest, and when evening falls they are dissolved into It again.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.18 With the coming of day all manifested things emerge from the Unmanifest and when night comes they merge in that itself which is called the Unmanifested.

records.sanskrit:
भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते।
रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥
records.iast:
bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate
rātryāgame.avaśaḥ pārtha prabhavatyaharāgame
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Yea! this vast company of living things--
  Again and yet again produced--expires
  At Brahma's Nightfall; and, at Brahma's Dawn,
  Riseth, without its will, to life new-born.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.19 This same multitude of beings, being born again and again, is dissolved, helplessly, O Arjuna (into the Unmanifested) at the coming of the night and comes forth at the coming of the day.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.19 The same multitude of beings, which have lived on earth so often, all are dissolved as the night of the universe approaches, to issue forth anew when morning breaks. Thus is it ordained.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.19 O son of Prtha, after being born again and again, that very multitude of beings disappears in spite of itself at the approach of night. It comes to life at the approach of day.

records.sanskrit:
परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः।
यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥
records.iast:
parastasmāttu bhāvo.anyo.avyakto.avyaktātsanātanaḥ
yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But--higher, deeper, innermost--abides
  Another Life, not like the life of sense,
  Escaping sight, unchanging. This endures
  When all created things have passed away:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.20 But verily there exists, higher than this Unmanifested, another unmanifested Eternal, which is not destroyed when all beings are destroyed.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.20 In truth, therefore, there is the Eternal Unmanifest, which is beyond and above the Unmanifest Spirit of Creation, which is never destroyed when all these being perish.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.20 But distinct from that Unmanifested is the other eternal unmainfest Reality, who does not get destroyed when all beings get destroyed.

records.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम्।
यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
records.iast:
avyakto.akṣara ityuktastamāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim
yaṃ prāpya na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
This is that Life named the Unmanifest,
  The Infinite! the All! the Uttermost.
  Thither arriving none return. That Life
  Is Mine, and I am there!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.21 What is called the Unmanifested and the Imperishable, That they say is the highest goal. They who reach It do not return (to this Samsara). That is My highest abode (place or state).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.21 The wise say that the Unmanifest and Indestructible is the highest goal of all; when once That is reached, there is no return. That is My Blessed Home.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.21 He who has been mentioned as the Unmanifested, the Immutable, they call Him the supreme Goal. That is the supreme abode of Mine, reaching which they do not return.

records.sanskrit:
पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया।
यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥
records.iast:
puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyastvananyayā
yasyāntaḥsthāni bhūtāni yena sarvamidaṃ tatam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And, Prince! by faith
  Which wanders not, there is a way to come
  Thither. I, the PURUSHA, I Who spread
  The Universe around me--in Whom dwell
  All living Things--may so be reached and seen!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.22 That highest Purusha, O Arjuna, is attainable by unswerving devotion to Him alone within Whom all beings dwell and by Whom all this is pervaded.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.22 O Arjuna! That Highest God, in Whom all beings abide, and Who pervades the entire universe, is reached only by wholehearted devotion. [The following material (between the asterisks) is an example of what may be a "doctored' inclusion. It does not jibe with the rest of the material because it is not presented as metaphor and clearly implies that worldly phenomena are spiritually determining. Maybe it was added by an individual or individuals who were less cognizant than the originating author. Or maybe was 'craftily' inserted to function as a sort of litmus test - those who get"taken in' by it may be recognized as not having "spiritual discernment'.]

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.22 O son of Prtha, that supreme Person-in whom are included (all) the beings and by whom all this is pervaded-is, indeed, reached through one-pointed devotion.

records.sanskrit:
यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः।
प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥
records.iast:
yatra kāle tvanāvṛttimāvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ
prayātā yānti taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold omits the five verses about departure paths and times. The source marks the gap with an ellipsis and an incorrectly repeated [FN#14]; translator note 15 explains the omitted ten Sanskrit lines.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.23 Now I will tell thee, O chief of Bharatas, the times departing at which the Yogis will return or not return.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.23 *Now I will tell thee, O Arjuna, of the times at which, if the mystics go forth, they do not return, and at which they go forth only to return.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.23 O best of the Bharata dynasty, I shall now speak of that time by departing at which the yogis attain the State of Non-return, and also (of the time by departing at which they attain) the State of Return.

records.sanskrit:
अग्निर्जोतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम्।
तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥
records.iast:
agnirjotirahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam
tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold omits the five verses about departure paths and times. The source marks the gap with an ellipsis and an incorrectly repeated [FN#14]; translator note 15 explains the omitted ten Sanskrit lines.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.24 Fire, light daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern path of the sun (the northern solstice) departing then (by these) men who know Brahman go to Brahman.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.24 If knowing the Supreme Spirit the sage goes forth with fire and light, in the daytime, in the fortnight of the waxing moon and in the six months before the Northern summer solstice, he will attain the Supreme.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.24 Fire, light, daytime, the birght forrnight, the six months of the Northern solstice-by following this Path, persons who are knowers of Brahman attain Brahman when they die.

records.sanskrit:
धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम्।
तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥
records.iast:
dhūmo rātristathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam
tatra cāndramasaṃ jyotiryogī prāpya nivartate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold omits the five verses about departure paths and times. The source marks the gap with an ellipsis and an incorrectly repeated [FN#14]; translator note 15 explains the omitted ten Sanskrit lines.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.25 Attaining to the lunar light by smoke, night time, the dark fortnight also, the six months of the southern path of the sun (the southern solstice), the Yogi returns.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.25 But if he departs in gloom, at night, during the fortnight of the waning moon and in the six months before the Southern solstice, then he reaches but lunar light and he will be born again.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.25 Smoke, night, as also the dark fortnight and the six months of the Southern solstice-following this Path the yogi having reached the lunar light, returns.

records.sanskrit:
शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते।
एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययावर्तते पुनः ॥
records.iast:
śuklakṛṣṇe gatī hyete jagataḥ śāśvate mate
ekayā yātyanāvṛttimanyayāvartate punaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold omits the five verses about departure paths and times. The source marks the gap with an ellipsis and an incorrectly repeated [FN#14]; translator note 15 explains the omitted ten Sanskrit lines.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.26 The bright and the dark paths of the world are verily thought to be eternal; by the one (the bright path) a man goes not to return and by the other (the dark path) he returns.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.26 These bright and dark paths out of the world have always existed. Whoso takes the former, returns not; he who chooses the latter, returns.*

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.26 These two courses of the world, which are white and black, are verily considered eternal. By the one a man goes to the State of Non-return; by the other he returns again.

records.sanskrit:
नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन।
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन ॥
records.iast:
naite sṛtī pārtha jānanyogī muhyati kaścana
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu yogayukto bhavārjuna
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.note: Arnold omits the five verses about departure paths and times. The source marks the gap with an ellipsis and an incorrectly repeated [FN#14]; translator note 15 explains the omitted ten Sanskrit lines.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.27 Knowing these paths, O Arjuna, no Yogi is deluded; therefore at all times be steadfast in Yoga.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.27 O Arjuna! The saint knowing these paths is not confused. Therefore meditate perpetually.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.27 O son of Prtha, no yogi [One steadfast in meditation.) whosoever has known these two courses becomes deluded. Therefore, O Arjuna, be you steadfast in yoga at all times.

records.sanskrit:
वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैव
दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम्।
अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वा
योगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् ॥
records.iast:
vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva dāneṣu yatpuṇyaphalaṃ pradiṣṭam
atyeti tatsarvamidaṃ viditvā yogī paraṃ sthānamupaiti cādyam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Richer than holy fruit on Vedas growing,
     Greater than gifts, better than prayer or fast,
  Such wisdom is! The Yogi, this way knowing,
     Comes to the Utmost Perfect Peace at last.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 8.28 Whatever fruit of merit is declared (in the scriptures) to accrue from (the study of) the Vedas, (the performance of) sacrifices, (the practice of) austerities, and gifts beyond all this goes the Yogi, having known this; and he attains to the Supreme Primeval (first or ancient) Abode.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 8.28 The sage who knows this passes beyond all merit that comes from the study of the scriptures, from sacrifice, from austerities and charity, and reaches the Supreme Primeval Abode."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 8.28 Having known this, the yogi transcends all those results of rigtheous deeds that are declared with regard to the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities and also charities, and he reaches the primordial supreme State.
